title: Permission Graph Explorer + Member Bulk Actions: RBAC v2 Console UX
creator: Nora Patel
description: Design a cohesive Console experience for RBAC v2 focused on two tightly coupled flows: a Permission Graph Explorer that visualizes role inheritance and effective permissions, and a Member Bulk Actions experience for assigning roles, previewing SSO/SAML group mappings, and scheduling changes. The page should integrate audit-log context and guardrails for admin controls so operators can safely make large-scale changes without introducing privilege escalation or compliance gaps.
background: RBAC v1 UI had separate role editor screens and a simple member list assignment modal. With RBAC v2 we need to show inheritance, conditional grants, and the interactions between SSO group mappings and manually assigned principals. Customers have asked for: (1) a way to preview "effective access" for a user before changing roles, (2) bulk assignment tooling to map groups from SSO to roles, and (3) clear visibility into which changes will be recorded in audit logs and why. This ticket covers the UX patterns and edge-case handling for those needs.
design_goals: Make effective permissions discoverable with minimal cognitive load
Enable safe bulk member operations with preview and dry-run mode
Surface SSO/SAML group mapping conflicts and allow non-destructive reconciliation
Show audit log linkage and change provenance inline with role edits
Provide admin guardrails: permission simulation, automatic conflict warnings, and a rollback plan
acceptance_criteria: Permission Graph Explorer mockups (desktop + tablet) exist with annotated states: default, filtered-by-resource, and filter-by-principal
Member Bulk Actions flow mockups showing: CSV/group import, match preview, conflict resolution UI, schedule apply, and dry-run simulation
A microcopy spec for warnings, tooltips, and audit messages is included
Prototype has an example of 'Simulate as' that shows effective read/write/list scopes for a selected principal
Design review sign-off from Security and PM is captured and items for a follow-up research spike are identified
out_of_scope: Full implementation of backend audit retention UI (only linking + messaging required)
On-prem offline CSV imports for air-gapped installs (defer to Private deployment docs)
Deep integration with Identity Provider UI — we only provide mapping preview and reconciliation in Console
deliverables: High-fidelity mockups for Permission Graph Explorer (3 filters)
Interaction spec for Member Bulk Actions and dry-run simulation
Handoff Figma file and component variants
Design notes for engineering edge cases (partial failures, retry semantics)
decisions: Show effective permissions as a flattened list with tags indicating origin (role, SSO group, direct assignment)
Implement a read-only dry-run preview that computes deltas but does not write to audit logs until user confirms
Bulk assignment will default to match on SSO group name, with a manual reconciliation step for mismatches
Permission Graph will permit filtering by resource type, permission action, and principal type (user/group/service-account)
Design will include an 'Impact Summary' overlay before apply that lists number of principals affected and top risky permissions (e.g., admin, iam:*)
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Admins may accidentally grant high-privilege roles in bulk. Mitigation: Add explicit risk badge and require additional confirmation for high-risk changes
Risk: SSO group mapping ambiguity leads to incorrect matches. Mitigation: Provide fuzzy-match preview + confidence score and require manual approve for low-confidence matches
Risk: Large bulk operations may partially fail. Mitigation: Recommend idempotent operations, show per-row status with retry and rollback guidance in UI
notes: PM feedback (2025-02-12): prefer schedule-apply over immediate apply for enterprise customers to align with change windows
Security review (2025-02-17): request explicit audit log copy when dry-run is promoted to apply; engineering to confirm feasibility
Design review (2025-02-19): accessibility check required for graph visualization; create text-only fallback and keyboard navigation plan

Evan Park (Eng) (2025-02-13): Backend can surface effective-permissions endpoint but needs a limit parameter; recommend batching for members >500
Liam Chen (Security) (2025-02-15): Suggest adding 'last evaluated' timestamp and link to the exact audit entry for the permission change
Nora Patel (Designer) (2025-02-18): Updated microcopy for high-risk confirmation modal per Security feedback
Marisol Ortega (2025-02-20): Pushed final mocks and prepared engineering handoff doc. Awaiting Security sign-off on audit copy requirement
next_steps: Schedule design-engr sync to review API contract for effective-permissions endpoint
Create accessibility task for graph keyboard interactions (estimate: 3)
Resolve audit-copy feasibility with backend team and update acceptance criteria
implementation_notes: Frontend should render origin badges (role | sso-group | direct) next to each permission line
Member bulk flow must support cancellation and produce an idempotent plan object that backend can execute or rollback
When a dry-run is converted to apply, the system should create an audit entry that references the dry-run ID for traceability
